RUSSL GFM TERMINAL — RELEASE 0.5 CORRECTION
Prepared 2026-10-11.

The default terminal now operates on mechanics datasets. It opens with raw
pendulum restoring-acceleration samples; their original magnitude and zero
values are retained. The default composer prepares, transforms, verifies and
records those data through gfm.* commands.

The primary controls offer two distinct domains:
  - Ordinary real/complex signals: q samples indexed by GF(q), transformed
    with the positive additive trace-character kernel and its inverse.
  - Exact field coefficients: q-1 GF(q) values evaluated at powers of a
    primitive field element, with exact inverse interpolation.

Field-coordinate oscillator and rational-rotation inspectors remain exact
algebraic mechanics. The GF80 word workbench, captures and bounded replay
remain available as a separate reversible mechanics workflow.

The original normalized-state lab is explicitly secondary Reference math.
Its probability, Wigner and mana tools retain their existing conventions and
separate state. Selecting GFM commands returns to the mechanics workspace.
Hiding Reference math also hides its Wigner display through return-tab changes.

Reapply equations and the GFM/horizon load actions now produce an original-
scale exterior-signal dataset, with inverse recovery checked. The saved report
also recalculates the raw pendulum and Mellin samples and all three ordinary
rotations from the supplied images. Exact polynomial examples cover all five
small fields; the zero passage example remains zero throughout its transform.

All 49 horizon findings, the 20 earlier findings and three prior image families
retain their audit dispositions and source attribution. Their domains stay
explicit. The gaseous-aperture/aggie scenario remains the user's hypothetical
simulation rule. The correction changes the terminal's executable data model;
it does not establish new gravitational or material laws.

Version 0.5 sessions contain the active mechanics dataset. Mechanics records
can be restored explicitly. Older sessions, source bytes, equation audits,
numeric reports and examples remain preserved under their original conventions.
Older normalized snapshots load into Reference math alongside default raw
mechanics data. Imported histories remain inert.

OPEN AND REVIEW
Open index.html or Open-Terminal.cmd after extracting the complete package.
Import examples/GFM-Mechanics-session.json from Evidence & ledger to load the
new recorded example. Restore its exact GF9 polynomial or zero-passage record
to inspect those domains directly.

README.txt provides commands and operating instructions.
docs/GFM_Terminal_Identity.txt states the current coefficient domains.
mechanics-reapplication.json contains the current saved calculations.
validation/verification-summary.json identifies the completed checks.
validation/tests-v0.5.txt contains the final full automated test output.
validation/mechanics-independent-verification.json binds the separate Python
mathematical checks to the exact saved files and preserved source identities.

Live browser rendering, actual downloads and live GF80 iframe communication
remain unverified. Mathematical, command and DOM checks cover their declared
scopes. Earlier output releases and original supplied files remain unchanged.
